items.q: A 14-year-old boy and a 14-year-old girl of identical height and identical serum creatinine are assessed with the Schwartz equation. Per the printed K values, the boy's eGFR will be:
opts: Higher, because K is 0.7 in adolescent boys versus 0.55 in adolescent girls
Lower, because K is 0.55 in adolescent boys
The same, since K varies with height and not with sex
Undefined, because K is printed only below 2 years of age
items.exp: The K constants are listed as: <1 yr pre-term 0.33, term 0.45; 1–2 yr & adolescent girls 0.55; adolescent boys 0.7. (Book p736)

items.q: Each Schwartz constant is paired with the correct group EXCEPT:
opts: Term infant <1 yr, age not mentioned — 0.45
items.exp: The 1–2 yr and adolescent girls line carries K = 0.55; 0.45 is the term infant value used when the age is not mentioned. (Book p736)

items.q: The Schwartz equation printed here estimates a child's GFR from body surface area divided by serum creatinine.
opts: False — it is K × length of the child ÷ S.Cr
True — BSA is the numerator of the printed formula
False — it uses weight rather than length
items.exp: The line reads: eGFR = K × length of child ÷ S.Cr, with K described as a constant. (Book p736)

items.q: The constant K in this equation is changed according to:
items.exp: K is tabulated by developmental group: pre-term, term, 1–2 yr and adolescent girls, adolescent boys — i.e. age plus sex, not any measured variable. (Book p736)
